editor_note:
Infrastructure lock-in entered its decisive phase. Anthropic's 300MW/$5B-per-year agreement with SpaceX's Colossus—backed by 8000% annualized ARR growth—confirms this is a utility business, not a research bet. SAP's $1.16B acquisition of 18-month-old Prior Labs, combined with restrictions on which AI agents customers may use, is the enterprise-software version of the same move: claim the AI layer before hyperscalers commoditize it. For pharma IT, the SAP play is the most consequential item this run—every S/4HANA instance in your stack is about to carry AI you didn't select.

The Latent Space services thesis explains the mechanism: AI is shifting from capability to delivered outcome, which means your vendor contracts and integration architecture now matter as much as the models. OpenAI's B2B Signals data confirms the early-mover gap is already compounding through agentic workflows.

GPT-5.x deriving novel results in quantum gravity is the leading-indicator story for pharma. If AI can produce original scientific work at the frontier, the drug-discovery co-pilot timeline just compressed by several years.
